title: Quantum Pack: microburst-reserve bundles, SLA laddering, and SQ automation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Proposal for a new SKU family (Quantum Pack) that bundles reserved GPU capacity with a deterministic microburst credit pool, tiered SLA laddering (latency-backed tiers), and an automated Security Questionnaire (SQ) routing workflow for faster enterprise procurement. Goal is to increase win-rate on enterprise Dedicated customers with spiky demand patterns while preserving predictable unit economics and defensible SLOs. This ticket captures pricing experiments, contract Q/A considerations, and the integrated SQ automation requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 Quantum Pack tiers (Baseline, Elastic, Resilient) with explicit reserved GPU units + burst credits and published pricing table
Run A/B pricing experiment with ~20 eligible prospects via Sales for 6 weeks and collect conversion and ARR delta
Legal approves contract addendum language for burst consumption, preemption and overage billing
Security team validates SQ automation flow (auto-route to tenant-specific reviewer, pre-populate answers from standard template)
Engineering confirms feasibility of quota and enforcement primitives for microburst credit accounting and graceful fallback to pre-specified model variants
experiment_matrix: Variants: A) Low price/high burst ratio (40% reserved/60% burst), B) Medium balanced (60/40), C) High reserve/low burst (80/20). Test metrics: conversion rate, ARR per customer, p99 latency violation frequency, avg cost per token under typical burst profile. Sales cohort segmentation by current committed customers with seasonal burstiness (games, media rendering, batch inference partners).
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize tier definitions and draft contract language with Legal
Week 2-4: Implement budget accounting hooks and telemetry (ENG-PR to instrument burst usage)
Week 4-10: Pilot with 15-25 customers through Sales AE cohort - collect signals
Week 10-12: Analyze results, iterate pricing or SKU definitions
Week 12+: Prepare GA docs, Console UI for purchasing, and pre-approved SQ templates
metrics: Incremental ARR per pilot customer (target > $50k annual)
SLA breach rate (p99 latency) during bursts (target < 1% increase)
Average unit cost during bursts (target within +15% of baseline)
Time-to-SQ-complete for enterprise deals (target reduce from 18 days to <7 days)
Number of customers adopting Quantum Pack vs legacy Dedicated SKUs
open_questions: How granular should microburst accounting be (per-minute windows vs per-request)?
Should burst credits be pooled across projects/orgs or isolated per-reservation?
What is the fair allocation policy when regional capacity is constrained (preemption vs throttling)?
Can we auto-convert sustained burst usage into a temporary elevated commit to avoid repeated overage billing?
What SLA credits or financial remedies trigger when burst-caused latency exceeds tier thresholds?
Is it feasible for Sales to sell a blended price by converting past observed burst metrics into recommended tier assignment?
risks_mitigations: Revenue leakage from poorly instrumented burst billing -> Mitigation: implement end-to-end telemetry and daily reconciliation reports
Customer confusion on burst semantics -> Mitigation: create clear Console UX and one-page factsheet and sample math showing cost scenarios
Operational capacity exhaustion during concentrated bursts -> Mitigation: region-level fallbacks to compatible model variants and enforced concurrency caps
Legal pushback on preemption language -> Mitigation: add explicit carve-outs, cooldown windows, and optional paid non-preemptible addons
Security questionnaire delays -> Mitigation: pre-approved, partially auto-filled SQ templates mapped to standard answers and fast-track reviewer list
